clue.text: Generally contemptible, he was nevertheless British

definitions.text: Generally contemptible, he was nevertheless British

parts.words: Generally contemptible, he was nevertheless British
parts.note: the General who led the Old Contemptibles, the British army of 1914, carried a surname suggesting a different nationality

explanation.surface: A grudging tribute to someone despised but patriotic.
explanation.walkthrough: Field Marshal Sir John French commanded the British Expeditionary Force of 1914, whose soldiers called themselves the Old Contemptibles; so a General of the Contemptibles was British despite his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The commander's surname was that of Britain's neighbouring nation across the Channel.

clue.text: Anticipate store trouble in autumn

indicators.note: one set of letters goes inside the word for the season

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: store is put into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Expecting trouble at the shop in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns STORE into OREST, which 'in' places inside FALL after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in advance so as to prevent something is to anticipate it.

clue.text: What 15 does to the listener in extremis

parts.note: at the extremity or end
the ears do the listening

explanation.surface: How absence affects someone who hears of it at the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is ABSENCE: the proverb 'absence makes the heart grow fonder' says what absence does.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence makes people dearer to each other, as the proverb about the fonder heart says.

clue.text: Captive flier lost touch with the van

definitions.text: Captive flier lost touch with the van

parts.words: Captive flier lost touch with the van
parts.note: the music-hall song where the singer follows the removal van carrying a caged songbird, then dawdles and loses the way

explanation.surface: A caged bird left behind by a moving van.
explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall song 'My Old Man Said Follow the Van' has the singer trailing the furniture van with 'my old ____ ____', then dilly-dallying and losing the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A male songbird of the finch family kept in a cage, as in the song.

clue.text: Where, unemployed and angry, statesmen take to flight

definitions.text: Where, unemployed and angry, statesmen take to flight

parts.note: someone out of work is idle
furious, as in wild with rage

explanation.surface: Jobless, furious politicians running away.
explanation.walkthrough: Idlewild was the name of New York's main airport (now JFK), where visiting statesmen board their planes; 'take to flight' sounds like fleeing but means flying off.
explanation.definitionFit: Idlewild was the former name of John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York, a departure point for flights.

clue.text: Servant of early church in second sea disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves the letters of second sea in ruins, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchwoman caught up in a second maritime calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: Women were ordained to serve as assistants to the clergy in the early Christian church.

clue.text: Enough to upset the Mayfair district

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting the words turns them upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Mayfair in London has the postal district W1, written W ONE

explanation.surface: Upsetting Mayfair's residents is plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is in London's W1 postcode; W ONE turned up gives the archaic word for enough.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic word meaning sufficient.

clue.text: Occupy, in horsy fashion

parts.note: a riding habit is the outfit worn on horseback

explanation.surface: Living like a horse lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To live in a place is to occupy it.

clue.text: "With mirth in funeral, and with——-in marriage" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "With mirth in funeral, and with——-in marriage" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "With mirth in funeral, and with——-in marriage" (Hamlet)
parts.note: Claudius's speech pairs opposites, so the gap needs a mournful song to contrast with marriage

explanation.surface: A quotation from Claudius on his hasty marriage to the widowed queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet I.ii Claudius says he married Gertrude 'with mirth in funeral and with ____ in marriage': the gap is a funeral song.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament sung at a funeral, the opposite of wedding mirth.

clue.text: Dressed in mid-second century Roman style

parts.note: the middle of the second century is year 150, CL in Roman numerals
AD, anno Domini, is the Latin style of dating years

explanation.surface: Wearing the fashion of second-century Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: AD 150, written the Roman way with CL, marks the middle of the second century.
explanation.definitionFit: To be clothed is to be wearing garments.

clue.text: Cad and liar, might the reactionary, call him?

definitions.text: Cad and liar, might the reactionary, call him?

indicators.note: the clue asks what the reactionary might make of these words, inviting the letters of cad and liar to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A conservative's abusive verdict on a political opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CAD and LIAR rearrange to the word the reactionary would use, and the whole clue is the reactionary's opinion of that person.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactionary despises an extreme reformer and would call such a progressive opponent names.

clue.text: Someone else with a refusal to take the right

parts.note: a refusal is a no

explanation.surface: Another person declines but accepts what is due.
explanation.definitionFit: A different person is one additional individual, as in 'ask somebody new'.

clue.text: Firm with an entrance in the mews

definitions.text: Firm with an entrance in the mews

parts.note: steady, secure, as in a stable base
a door is a way in

explanation.surface: A company whose premises open onto a mews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a business, but it is the adjective STABLE; a mews was originally a row of stables, so the door there is a stable door.
explanation.definitionFit: A mews is a yard of stables, and the way into each stall is through its own door.

clue.text: Liszt took orders for these notes

definitions.text: Liszt took orders for these notes

parts.words: Liszt took orders for these notes
parts.note: the composer took minor holy orders and gained a clerical title, which is also spelt by four musical notes

explanation.surface: The composer accepting commissions for some music.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Liszt took minor orders in 1865 and was known as the Abbé Liszt; the title is spelt with the notes A, B, B and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title for a cleric, held by the composer after he entered minor orders.

clue.text: Not however one of those ring-a-ring roses

definitions.text: Not however one of those ring-a-ring roses

parts.words: Not however one of those ring-a-ring roses
parts.note: a bloom whose name suggests something that rings, yet is no rose from the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A remark about the flowers in a children's singing game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring-a-ring o' roses' is the nursery rhyme; the flower in question rings like a bell but is not a rose.
explanation.definitionFit: The campanula is a plant with bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: I ac leave this without leave

definitions.text: I ac leave this without leave

parts.words: I ac leave this without leave
parts.note: a leading aircraftman who goes away without permission is said to be away without leave, the AWOL offence

explanation.surface: A serviceman slipping off without permission.
explanation.walkthrough: LAC is a leading aircraftman in the RAF; the military offence AWOL is 'absent without leave', and taking an unauthorised break means taking this without leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away from duty or a place is the state of not being present there.

clue.text: Look-out man

parts.note: a sentry is a look-out man, but read literally it is a person whose attention turns outward

explanation.walkthrough: A look-out is a watchman; but a man who looks out, toward others, is an outgoing personality.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person directs attention outside the self.

clue.text: His is the kiss of life in politics

definitions.text: His is the kiss of life in politics

parts.words: His is the kiss of life in politics
parts.note: a kiss is written X, the cross a voter marks on a ballot paper, which keeps a politician alive

explanation.surface: A political saviour reviving a failing cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The kiss is the cross (X) on a ballot paper: each voter's X gives politicians their life.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter marks a cross on the ballot, and those marks decide which politicians survive.

clue.text: Savoir conduire

parts.note: a French-style phrase on the model of savoir faire, meaning know-how about driving

explanation.walkthrough: Savoir faire is social know-how; savoir conduire (French: to know how to drive) is the motorist's equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: Good judgement of traffic and road conditions is a driver's know-how.

clue.text: Thrash the grass till it's aglow

parts.note: to lam is to beat soundly
bent is a type of grass

explanation.surface: Beating the lawn until it shines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes a light or flame that flickers softly and glows.

clue.text: Improper control of the old Christmas revels

definitions.meaning: the medieval festivities presided over by a mock Lord chosen for the season

explanation.surface: Disorderly authority at a traditional Christmas party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lord of Misrule presided over Christmas festivities in medieval and Tudor England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad government, and the riotous Christmas season led by a mock lord.

clue.text: No peach, in the harem

parts.note: a dried fruit that is a grape rather than a peach, and also a ruler's wife living in the harem

explanation.surface: A harem woman who is no beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peach' looks like slang for a pretty woman; the answer is both a dried grape (not a peach) and the wife of a sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a seedless raisin and the wife of a Muslim ruler, who would live in the harem.

clue.text: Pressure gauge provides the emperor with outside help

indicators.note: the help word stands outside the emperor, wrapping round him

parts.note: aid is help
Nero was the Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An instrument giving an emperor support.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer that measures air pressure without using liquid.

clue.text: To overtake you need a little sleight of hand

definitions.meaning: to go by another vehicle on the road
a conjuror's single movement of the hands over an object

explanation.surface: A driver needing a deft touch to get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers go by slower cars, and magicians make a deft hand movement over a card or coin.

clue.text: A little bit — of fluff perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a bit of fluff is slang for an attractive young woman, also called a bit of stuff

explanation.surface: A tiny fragment of fluff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of fluff' is old slang for an attractive girl; the answer is another word for a bit, giving 'piece of fluff' too.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion of something, and old slang for a young woman.

clue.text: Marco and Giuseppe, that crafty pair!

definitions.text: Marco and Giuseppe, that crafty pair!

parts.words: Marco and Giuseppe, that crafty pair!
parts.note: the two Venetian boatmen heroes of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera, crafty because their craft are boats

explanation.surface: Two sly Italians up to tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: Marco and Giuseppe are the heroes of the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta of that title; 'crafty' means working small craft, not sly.
explanation.definitionFit: The two brothers in the operetta row Venetian boats for a living.

clue.text: Filled last summer as well as in February

definitions.text: Filled last summer as well as in February

parts.words: Filled last summer as well as in February
parts.note: the country saying calls February the month that fills ditches with rain or snow, and last summer was wet too

explanation.surface: A remark on a wet summer and a wet February.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'February fill-dyke' names the month that fills the ditches; the clue says a rainy summer filled them as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditch for drainage, which fills with water in wet weather.

clue.text: The main point is in the type of car

indicators.note: the little word goes inside the car abbreviation

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a type of sports car

explanation.surface: Getting to the heart of a car's design.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence or substance of an argument.

clue.text: Sir Percy playing hard-to get

parts.note: Sir Percy Blakeney, the Scarlet Pimpernel, was the 'demmed' hard-to-catch hero of Baroness Orczy's verse

explanation.surface: A gentleman feigning coyness.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Percy Blakeney is the Scarlet Pimpernel: 'Is he in heaven? Is he in hell? That demmed, ____ Pimpernel.'
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard to catch or pin down slips away from its pursuers.

clue.text: Where in the Orient a cow is heard to get the bird

indicators.note: the clue says the cow is only heard, so its spoken sound gives the letters

parts.note: the farm animal, spelt differently for its sound
a loon is a diving bird, the North American name for a diver

explanation.surface: A cow that somehow ends up catching a bird in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Kowloon is the peninsula of Hong Kong facing the island, a place in the Far East.

clue.text: Sloth, for example, in garden and gallery

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Laziness in a garden and an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' reads as the sin of idleness; here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloths belong to the order of toothless mammals along with anteaters and armadillos.

clue.text: A development of pontoon ?

parts.note: pontoon is a card game, and also a floating support from which a river crossing is built

explanation.surface: A card game evolving from another one.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is a card game, so a card game developed from it is suggested; but a pontoon (float) is built up into a crossing, and that crossing shares its name with another card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontoon float supports a temporary river crossing, which shares its name with a card game.
